api.orthanc_credentials_missing: ORTHANC_ADMIN_USER and ORTHANC_ADMIN_PASS are not set in .env: the route answers but cannot call Orthanc.
api.settings_dir_not_writable: Settings directory is not writable ({error}). Check that '{dir}' is mounted read-write on auth-service.
api.env_not_mounted: The .env file is not reachable from the container. Add the './.env:/host/env/.env:rw' mount to the auth-service service, then recreate the container.
api.public_url_https: The public address must start with https://
api.public_url_no_host: The public address has no host name.
api.public_url_path: Give the origin only, without a path (for example https://pacs.example.org).
api.public_url_no_dot: '{host}' contains no dot: browsers will reject the session cookie. Use a fully qualified name (pacs.example.org) or pacs.localhost.
api.authelia_config_host_missing: No trace of '{host}' in configuration.yml: the file was edited by hand, change aborted.
api.users_file_corrupt: users_database.yml is corrupt: {error}. Restore a backup from the panel's Backups tab.
api.orthanc_section_missing: {setting}: section {section} missing from the file, add it manually first.
api.orthanc_file_corrupt: orthanc.json is corrupt: {error}. Restore a backup from the panel's Backups tab.
api.active_admin_required: At least 1 active admin required, otherwise nobody can administer anymore.
api.password_not_argon2: {user}: password must be an argon2id hash (starting with $argon2id$).
api.file_locked: File locked by another administrator, try again in 5 s.
api.group_required: A group is required: an account without a group can sign in but has access to nothing. Accepted values: {accepted}.
api.group_unknown: Unknown group(s): {unknown}. Accepted values: {accepted}. A group missing from Authelia's rules gives an account that signs in but gets 403 on everything.
api.group_single: One group per account (received: {received}). The three roles are exclusive: Authelia applies the first matching rule, so combining them restricts nothing, it widens access.
api.username_invalid: Username: 3 to 64 characters among letters, digits and . _ % + -, optionally followed by an e-mail domain.
api.orthanc_container_not_found: Container '{container}' not found. Check ORTHANC_CONTAINER in the compose file.
api.docker_proxy_refused: The Docker proxy refused the restart (HTTP {status}). Check ALLOW_RESTARTS on the socket-proxy service.
api.setup_already_done_use_accounts: Setup is already complete: use account management instead.
api.setup_admin_exists: An administrator already exists: complete the setup, then use account management to add more.
api.address_in_use_setup: The address {address} is already in use. It identifies the account and cannot be used twice.
api.password_is_login: The password cannot be the account's address: it is the first thing an attacker tries.
api.address_in_use_other: The address {address} is already used by another account. It is the login: it cannot be shared.
api.last_admin_change: This change would leave no active administrator: {user} is the last one. Removing them from the admin group, or disabling them, would leave the installation without any administration.
api.cannot_delete_self: You cannot delete your own account.
api.last_admin_delete: {user} is the last active administrator: deleting them would leave the installation without any administration, and the only way back would be editing users_database.yml by hand. Create another administrator first.
api.orthanc_change_invalid: Invalid orthanc.json change, nothing was written: {error}
api.orthanc_change_mismatch: The orthanc.json change does not match what was requested, nothing was written.
api.orthanc_reload_rollback_failed: Reloading Orthanc failed ({error}). The automatic rollback failed too ({rollback_error}). Inconsistent state, manual restore required: backup={backup}
api.orthanc_reload_rolled_back: Reloading Orthanc failed ({error}). Automatically rolled back from {backup}: the configuration is back to its previous state.
api.restart_unavailable: Restart unavailable: DOCKER_PROXY_URL is not set. Enable the socket-proxy service, or restart by hand with 'docker compose restart orthanc'.
api.orthanc_down_no_backup: Orthanc has not answered for 60 s and no backup of its configuration is available. Check its logs (docker compose logs orthanc).
api.orthanc_down_restore_failed: Orthanc is not answering, and restoring {backup} failed ({error}). Manual intervention required.
api.orthanc_config_refused_restored: Orthanc did not restart with the new configuration: {backup} was restored and it answers again. The change is refused, the PACS is back in service.
api.orthanc_still_down: Orthanc is still not answering after restoring {backup}. The cause therefore lies elsewhere than in the last change. Check its logs (docker compose logs orthanc).
api.cf_enforce_incomplete: Enforcing requires both the team domain and the audience: without them every upload would answer 503.
api.session_block_missing: No top-level 'session:' block in the Authelia configuration.
api.duration_invalid: {key}: '{value}' is not an Authelia duration: a number followed by s, m, h, d, w, M or y, for example 15m or 1h30m.
api.session_reread_mismatch: {key} re-read as {got} instead of {value}, nothing was written.
api.authelia_config_locked: Authelia configuration is locked, try again.
api.backup_not_found: Backup not found or invalid name.
api.orthanc_help.Name: Name of this instance, shown in the interface and announced to other servers.
api.orthanc_help.DicomAet: DICOM identifier of this server (Application Entity Title). It is the name modalities must know to send it images.
api.orthanc_help.RemoteAccessAllowed: Allows API access from a machine other than the server itself. Required here, since nginx runs in another container.
api.orthanc_help.DicomServerEnabled: Enables the DICOM service. Without it, no modality can send images directly.
api.orthanc_help.DicomPort: DICOM listening port. 4242 by convention; declare the same value on the modalities.
api.orthanc_help.DicomCheckCalledAet: Refuses connections whose called AET does not match ours. Protects against misaddressed sends.
api.orthanc_help.DicomAlwaysAllowEcho: Accepts connectivity tests (C-ECHO) from any device, even unknown. Harmless: no data is exchanged.
api.orthanc_help.DicomAlwaysAllowStore: Accepts IMAGE SENDS from any device, even undeclared. Convenient, but lets anyone store on the PACS if they reach the DICOM port.
api.orthanc_help.DicomAlwaysAllowFind: Accepts QUERIES from an undeclared device. A query reveals patient names.
api.orthanc_help.DicomAlwaysAllowMove: Accepts TRANSFER requests from an undeclared device: it can have studies sent to itself.
api.orthanc_help.DicomScpTimeout: Delay, in seconds, before giving up on an incoming DICOM connection that stopped answering.
api.orthanc_help.DicomThreadsCount: Number of DICOM connections handled simultaneously.
api.orthanc_help.DicomModalitiesInDatabase: Keeps the list of modalities in the database rather than in the configuration file. Required for the Devices tab to survive a restart.
api.orthanc_help.OrthancPeersInDatabase: Same for the list of paired Orthanc servers.
api.orthanc_help.StorageCompression: Compresses stored files. Saves space, costs computing time on every read and write.
api.orthanc_help.MaximumStorageSize: Maximum storage size, in MB. 0 = unlimited. Beyond it, Orthanc deletes according to MaximumStorageMode.
api.orthanc_help.MaximumPatientCount: Maximum number of patients kept. 0 = unlimited.
api.orthanc_help.MaximumStorageMode: What is deleted when a limit above is reached: the oldest studies, or nothing (new sends are then refused).
api.orthanc_help.StoreMD5ForAttachments: Computes a checksum of each file to detect corruption. Costs computing time on write.
api.orthanc_help.HttpPort: Port of the web interface and API. nginx connects to it; changing it requires adjusting nginx.
api.orthanc_help.HttpTimeout: Delay, in seconds, before giving up on an HTTP request.
api.orthanc_help.HttpCompressionEnabled: Compresses HTTP responses. WARNING: nginx injects the 'Shares' and 'Administration' entries into the Orthanc Explorer menu by text substitution, which is impossible on a compressed response. Enabling this makes both entries disappear, with no other sign.
api.orthanc_help.StableAge: Delay, in seconds, without a new image before a study is considered complete. This is what triggers end-of-exam processing.
api.orthanc_help.OverwriteInstances: What to do when an image already present is received again: replace it, or ignore the send.
api.orthanc_help.ConcurrentJobs: Number of background jobs run in parallel (sends, anonymisations, archives).
api.orthanc_help.JobsHistorySize: Number of completed jobs kept in the history.
api.orthanc_help.SaveJobs: Keeps running jobs across a restart, instead of losing them.
api.orthanc_help.SynchronousCMove: Waits for a transfer to finish before answering the modality. Some older devices require it.
api.orthanc_help.LogLevel: Log verbosity. 'verbose' or 'trace' help with diagnosis, but fill the disk.
api.orthanc_help.DeidentifyLogs: Masks patient identifiers in the logs. Leave it on: logs are often read, copied and passed around.
api.orthanc_help.DefaultEncoding: Character set assumed when an image declares none. Latin1 for older European equipment, UTF-8 otherwise.
api.orthanc_help.LimitFindResults: Maximum number of results returned by a query. Protects against an overly broad query that would stall the server.
api.orthanc_help.LimitFindInstances: Same limit, applied at the image level.
api.orthanc_help.IngestTranscoding: Recompresses images to this format on reception. Saves space, but transforms the data on arrival.
api.orthanc_help.IngestTranscodingOfUncompre: Also applies this recompression to images that arrive uncompressed.
api.orthanc_help.DicomWeb.Enable: Enables DICOMweb. Essential: it is how the OHIF viewer reads images.
api.orthanc_help.DicomWeb.Root: Base path of the DICOMweb API. Must match what nginx proxies and what OHIF's app-config calls.
api.orthanc_help.DicomWeb.EnableWado: Enables WADO-URI, the older image retrieval protocol. Still used by some viewers.
api.orthanc_help.DicomWeb.StowMaxInstances: Maximum number of images accepted in a single STOW-RS send.
api.orthanc_help.DicomWeb.StowMaxSize: Maximum size, in MB, of a STOW-RS send.
api.orthanc_help.DicomWeb.EnableMetadata: Exposes DICOMweb metadata, which the viewer needs to display a study without downloading every image.
api.orthanc_help.DicomWeb.PublicRoot: DICOMweb URL as the BROWSER sees it, which differs from the internal path behind a proxy.
api.orthanc_help.AcceptedTransferSyntaxes: Compression formats accepted on reception. Narrowing this list refuses images arriving in another format.
api.session_label.expiration: Maximum length of a session, even an active one.
api.session_label.inactivity: Automatic sign-out after this long without activity.
api.persistence_flag_off: {flag} cannot be switched back to false: what was entered through the interface would be lost on restart.
api.address_in_use_active: The address {address} is already used by an active account. It identifies the account: it cannot be used twice. Edit the existing account, or delete it before recreating the address.
api.address_in_use_disabled: The address {address} is already used by a disabled account. It identifies the account: it cannot be used twice. Re-enable the existing account, or delete it before recreating the address.
api.orthanc_saved_not_running_file: Saved, but Orthanc is not running on this file: its image merges /etc/orthanc/*.json with the ORTHANC__* variables into a copy at startup, and that copy is what a reload re-reads. Restart the orthanc container for the change to take effect.
api.orthanc_restarted_divergent: Orthanc restarted, but {count} setting(s) are not applied as written. An ORTHANC__* variable in the compose file is probably overriding them.
api.session_keys_absent: Keys absent from the session block, nothing written: {keys}
api.session_written_restart: Durations written. Authelia only re-reads its accounts file, not its own configuration: restart it to apply — docker compose restart authelia
api.nothing_backed_up: No file could be backed up: {reasons}
api.share_role_forbidden: Your role does not allow creating a share link.
api.expiration_past: The expiration date (ExpirationDate) is already in the past.

admin.title: Administration
admin.role_admin: Administrator — full access and administration panel
admin.role_doctor: Doctor — view, upload and share studies
admin.help_new_password: At least twelve characters. It is the only thing between the Internet and patient images: this installation has no second factor. Prefer a long phrase to a short complicated word: it is stronger and easier to remember.
admin.password_relogin: The person will have to sign in again.
admin.edit_note: Removing the last active administrator from the admin group, or disabling them, is refused: the installation would be left with nobody to administer it.
admin.lock_reason: Last active administrator: disabling or deleting them would close the administration panel to everyone, and there is no back door — you would have to go back through SSH on the server. Appoint a second administrator first. The name and address can still be edited.
admin.account_renamed: Account renamed: sign-in now uses {new}, no longer {old}. The password is unchanged.
admin.confirm_enable: Enable '{name}'? The person will be able to sign in again.
admin.confirm_disable: Disable '{name}'? The account is kept, but the person will no longer be able to sign in.
admin.confirm_delete_user: Permanently delete the user '{name}'? A backup of the file is kept.
admin.password_too_short: Password too short: {count} character(s), at least 12 are required. A long phrase beats a complicated word.
admin.password_is_login: The password cannot be the account's address.
admin.confirm_password:
Replace the password of {name}?

The person will no longer be able to sign in with the old one, and will have to use the new one you just entered.
admin.password_changed: Password of {name} replaced. Give it to the person through a secure channel: it is shown nowhere and cannot be read back.
admin.account_created: Account created. Authelia re-reads the file automatically.
admin.orthanc_note: Orthanc does not read this file directly: its image makes a copy of it at startup. A change only applies after the container restarts, and the PACS is unavailable for a few seconds. If the new configuration prevents it from starting again, the last backup is restored automatically.
admin.divergences: {count} setting(s) are not applied as written.
admin.divergences_detail: An ORTHANC__* variable in the compose file may be overriding them, or Orthanc has not restarted since the last change.
admin.orthanc_written_restart: Written (backup {backup}). Orthanc reads a copy made at startup: click 'Restart Orthanc' to apply.
admin.confirm_restart: Restart Orthanc? The PACS will be unavailable for a few seconds. If the configuration prevents it from starting again, the last backup is restored automatically.
admin.modalities_intro: The ultrasound machines, scanners and other devices allowed to send exams. The declaration is stored in the database: it takes effect immediately, without restarting Orthanc.
admin.help_modality_name: Label shown in the list. Purely informative: it is not what identifies the device on the DICOM network, the AET is.
admin.help_aet: Application Entity Title: the DICOM name of the remote device. It must match EXACTLY what is configured on it, case included, otherwise the connection is refused.
admin.title_aet: 16 characters maximum, required by the DICOM standard
admin.help_host: IP address or name of the remote device, as the Orthanc server can reach it.
admin.help_port: DICOM port the remote device listens on. 104 or 11112 depending on the manufacturer.
admin.confirm_delete_modality: Delete the device '{name}'? It will no longer be able to send exams.
admin.cf_intro: Cloudflare validates the service token at its edge and does not pass it on: it relays a signed assertion, which this server checks against the team's public keys. The token itself is not entered here: it is rotated in Cloudflare, and nothing on this side has to follow. What is set here is what this server pins.
admin.help_cf_team_domain: Cloudflare Zero Trust domain, in the form myteam.cloudflareaccess.com. It pins the accepted issuer: without it, an assertion signed by any other Cloudflare team would be valid.
admin.help_cf_aud: Identifier of the Cloudflare Access application protecting DICOM upload. It pins the recipient: an assertion issued for another application of the same team is refused.
admin.help_cf_verification: When enabled, nginx requires a valid Cloudflare assertion on /api-upload/. Only enable it once the team domain AND the audience are set, otherwise every upload is refused.
admin.cf_enforce_note: Unchecked, uploads rely only on Cloudflare's filtering: no check is made here. Any request reaching the server another way would be accepted.
admin.cf_not_enforced: Verification is not active: uploads depend only on Cloudflare's filtering, with no check at the origin.
admin.cf_not_configured: Cloudflare Access is not configured: programmatic uploads (/api-upload/, Windows import workstation) are refused. Nothing to do if you do not use Cloudflare; otherwise fill in the team domain and the audience below.
admin.cf_aud_required: Enter the audience: it comes back masked, so it must be entered in full on every save.
admin.cf_saved: Cloudflare Access saved. Takes effect immediately, no restart.
admin.network_intro: The address this PACS is reached at. It appears once in .env and eleven times in Authelia's configuration: every access rule, plus the session cookie domain. Missing a single one is enough for Authelia to answer 401 on everything, sign-in page included. That is why it is set here and not by hand.
admin.network_note: Applies once you run sh scripts/apply.sh on the server (it restarts what needs it), then sign in again at the new address: the session cookie is tied to the old one. A port in the address becomes the port the PACS listens on.
admin.network_not_editable: Change unavailable: the .env file is not mounted in the container. Add './.env:/host/env/.env:rw' to the auth-service service, then recreate the container.
admin.confirm_network: Point the PACS to {url}? Authelia and .env are rewritten, a backup is taken first. Then run sh scripts/apply.sh on the server and sign in again at the new address.
admin.network_updated: {count} occurrence(s) updated. Run sh scripts/apply.sh on the server to apply.
admin.session_intro: Authelia format: a number followed by its unit (s, m, h, d), for example 15m, 1h or 1h30m. Authelia only re-reads its accounts file, not its own configuration: a restart is needed to apply.
admin.session_written: Written (backup {backup}). Authelia does not re-read its configuration: restart the container to apply — docker compose restart authelia
admin.backups_intro: A copy is taken before every change, and the last 10 are kept per file. For accounts, the contents of each backup are shown: that is what lets you pick the right one. Restoring replaces the file — the current state is backed up along the way, so the operation stays reversible.
admin.confirm_restore: Restore {target} from {name}? The current contents will be replaced, but they are backed up first: the operation stays reversible.
admin.restored_restart: {target} restored. Orthanc reads a copy made at startup: click 'Restart Orthanc' in the Orthanc configuration tab to apply.
admin.audit_intro: The last 200 events: accounts, Orthanc configuration, restored backups, restarts and requests rejected for security reasons. Kept in Redis, so lost if its volume is.
